top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock (Katori and Ye) rests on one clear idea, a magic-wavelength trap that does not shift the clock transition, and its 10^-18 performance has been checked by direct comparison between independent laboratories, which is the robustness I require. It already gives physics results (gravitational redshift over millimetres, limits on drifting constants and dark matter), and the two-name allocation is traceable. Twisted bilayer graphene (P001) is a worthy and reproduced discovery, but the pairing mechanism is open, the field is young and the Andrei and Cao attribution question is unresolved, so I rank it second. A prize is clearly better than no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; I work in atomic theory and have collaborated with Lund and ETH attosecond groups, not with Katori, Ye or the twisted-graphene authors.
